_about: What a phone's accelerometer does, as data. metasec polls MS.b(0x1000013) every 10 s and reports the samples taken since the last poll under 'acc' in report field /#9/#3 (doc/mssdk-report-fields.md); only sampling slot 1 is written, so gyro/euler stay empty and the accelerometer carries the whole signal. Motion.java generates the series from this file and holds no numbers of its own: the physics (gravity projected onto the device's attitude) is the algorithm, every quantity is here.
_source: the recorded phone's own samples (fp_values_full.json msb 0x1000013: -0.01,0.36,9.79 / -0.02,0.36,9.80) are 1 g at a constant 2.11 deg from flat, i.e. a phone lying still on a table. Those are the resting case below; the moving cases are the physics of a phone being held and carried, not measurements of this model, so they are stated as ranges rather than claimed as recorded values.
_warning: Replaying the recorded answers is what this replaces: ProfileJni clamps to the last recorded answer, so after the third poll the device reports the same two vectors for the rest of the session - an accelerometer that stopped while the app kept being used.
_gravity: standard gravity, the scale the accelerometer reports on; every sample's magnitude is built from it
_sample_ms: the interval between samples inside a poll window. The recording returned 1-2 samples per 10 s poll, so the device samples at about this rate for reporting purposes (not the sensor's own hardware rate).
_max_samples_per_poll: however long the gap before a poll, the device's buffer holds only so many
_first_poll_empty: the recording's first poll answered null: metasec's buffer had not filled yet. Ours does the same so the series starts the way the device's does.

resting_attitude._: flat on a table or a desk, give or take the surface's own wobble
in a hand, or leaning against something
propped up on a stand, nearly standing

_resting_attitude: where an owner happens to leave the phone, in degrees from flat. Drawn once per install: it is that person's habit, not a per-request value.
_initial_activity: what the phone is doing when a session starts - being looked at, or sitting where it was left

resting._: on a surface: one attitude, only the sensor's own noise on top. A phone on a table does not start walking by itself.

held._: in a hand, the owner reading: the attitude drifts and a hand is never quite still

walking._: carried: the step cadence loads and unloads the whole vector around 1 g

_activities: noise = per-sample noise (m/s^2); drift = how fast the attitude itself wanders (radians/s); stickiness = the chance a poll window keeps this activity; transitions = what it becomes when it does not (shares, summing to 1).
_stride: a walking cadence is about two steps a second; the amplitude is how far the magnitude swings either side of 1 g over a stride. Consecutive samples of one walk share a phase, so a walk reads as a walk rather than as independent noise.
_settle_tilt: put down: the phone comes to rest at a new attitude, not the one it had in the hand
